artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a prime $p$, let $\mathbb{F}_p$ denote the field with $p$ elements. Call a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ a sumset if there exists $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ with $S = A + A := \{a_1 + a_2 : a_1, a_2 \in A\}$. Define
$$M(p) := \max\{|S| : S \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p,\ S \neq A+A \text{ for every } A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p\}.$$
It is known that there exist absolute constants $c, C > 0$ such that, for all sufficiently large primes $p$,
$$p - C\, p^{2/3}(\log p)^{1/3} \;<\; M(p) \;<\; p - c\, p^{1/2}(\log p)^{1/2}.$$
Determine the correct order of $p - M(p)$ as $p \to \infty$; in particular, close the gap between these lower and upper bounds.
artifact.category_tag: Additive combinatorics / sumsets in finite fields
artifact.status_search_result: Alon established the bounds $p - C p^{2/3}(\log p)^{1/3} < M(p) < p - c p^{1/2}(\log p)^{1/2}$ and suggested the upper bound is closer to the truth. Subsequent literature (e.g., Alon–Granville on counting sumsets in $\mathbb{F}_p$) addresses related counting questions but does not appear to have closed this gap, and the problem is listed among contributed open problems in additive combinatorics.

status_evidence.snippet: Alon proves bounds on the largest subset of F_p that is not of the form A+A, with a gap between p - O(p^{2/3}(log p)^{1/3}) and p - Ω(p^{1/2}(log p)^{1/2}).
status_evidence.claim: Best known bounds, gap not yet closed.

status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up work studies counting of sumsets in F_p but does not resolve the extremal size question.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not close the gap.
